## What this document does

This notebook isolates the nitrogen question: fixed nitrogen levels run on
the whole-tree (`organ_level_sugar = FALSE`) sugar pathway, compared
against real observed SMEAR II height (Section 3). Section 4 reruns the
same nitrogen levels on the organ-level sugar pathway
(`organ_level_sugar = TRUE`), where `nitrogen_balance` is a genuinely
depleting/replenishing pool rather than a frozen input, to look at the
within-year (and across-year) nitrogen dynamics that mechanism actually
produces. Moved out of `height_correction.Rmd` (which now only covers the
non-nitrogen height/diameter-vs-observations baseline) so the two
questions don't share one notebook.

```{r libraries}
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)

pub_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom")
obs_col <- "#762a83"   # purple: observed, matches height_correction.Rmd's pub figure
```

## 1  Setup

### 1.1  Parameters

Same `h0`/`D0` overrides as `height_correction.Rmd`/`sugar_calibration.Rmd`'s
long-run scenario, so all three notebooks start the simulated tree at the
same point (12m height, matching the real stand's 1998 starting height
below).

```{r setup-data}
data_directory  <- "~/Documents/CASSIA_Calibration/Processed_Data/"
loaded_data     <- load_data(data_directory)

new_parameters  <- rep(0.5, 27)
parameters_2015 <- initialize_parameters(calibration = FALSE, new_parameters)

parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("h0"),          "Hyde"] <- 12
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("D0"),          "Hyde"] <- 0.1646  # back-extrapolated from real "BA weighted mean DBH pine" 2001/2008 (0.1737/0.1950m) - see manuscript/paper_plan.Rmd Working Notes
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_mean"),    "Hyde"] <- 463.8833
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_initial"), "Hyde"] <- 460.0
```

### 1.2  Weather data (1998-2022)

```{r setup-weather}
weather_preles <- data.table::fread("~/Documents/CASSIA/data/ERA5_CASSIA_preles.csv")

weather_1998_2022 <- weather_preles[
  weather_preles$date >= as.Date("1998-01-01") &
  weather_preles$date <= as.Date("2022-12-31"), ]
weather_1998_2022$dates <- as.Date(weather_1998_2022$date)

dates_1998_2022 <- weather_1998_2022$dates
```

### 1.3  Observed stand data (SMEAR II)

Real basal-area-weighted mean pine height and diameter at Hyytiälä - field
inventory data, not model output.

```{r load-biomass}
filter_smear <- function(vars) {
  loaded_data$smearII_data[loaded_data$smearII_data$variable %in% vars, ]
}

height_df   <- filter_smear(c("dominant_height",
                              "pine height BA weighted mean",
                              "pine height arithmetic mean",
                              "tree_height_baseal_area_weighted_mean"))
diameter_df <- filter_smear(c("BA weighted mean DBH pine",
                              "Arithmetic mean DBH pine",
                              "pine DBH arithmetic mean",
                              "pine diameter BA weighted mean"))

# Keep only the primary measurement for cleaner scenario plots
height_df   <- height_df[height_df$variable == "tree_height_baseal_area_weighted_mean", ]
diameter_df <- diameter_df[diameter_df$variable == "pine diameter BA weighted mean", ]

obs_height <- data.frame(
  dates = as.Date(paste0(height_df$date, "-12-31")),
  value = height_df$amount
)
obs_diameter <- data.frame(
  dates = as.Date(paste0(diameter_df$date, "-12-31")),
  value = diameter_df$amount / 100  # cm -> m, to match culm_growth_diameter's units
)
```

---

## 2  How nitrogen can limit growth

Two mechanisms exist in the C++ for nitrogen to constrain growth, and only
one of them runs in this notebook.

**What this notebook actually exercises** (`organ_level_sugar = FALSE`):
a per-day capacity gate. `nitrogen_balance` is a *fixed input* for the
whole run - nothing in this pathway ever changes it. Each day,
`nitrogen_storage()` (`sugar_model.cpp`) turns it into a capacity fraction
by comparing it against a hardcoded organ constant (4.0 for the
whole-tree "all" case used here), and `actual_growth()` applies that
fraction as `min(sugar_storage, nitrogen_capacity)` - whichever resource,
carbon or nitrogen, is scarcer on a given day wins.

```{r nitrogen-gate-diagram, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('
<pre class="mermaid">
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NitrogenChange

    state "nitrogen_change" as NitrogenChange <<choice>>
    NitrogenChange --> CapacityOne : FALSE, Control
    NitrogenChange --> NitrogenStorage : TRUE, High Medium or Low

    CapacityOne : nitrogen_capacity = 1.0
    CapacityOne : nitrogen_balance value is never read

    NitrogenStorage : nitrogen_storage function
    NitrogenStorage : ratio = nitrogen_balance divided by capacity_const
    NitrogenStorage --> RatioCheck

    state "ratio at least 1.0" as RatioCheck <<choice>>
    RatioCheck --> CapacityOne2 : yes
    RatioCheck --> CapacityRatio : no

    CapacityOne2 : nitrogen_capacity = 1.0
    CapacityOne2 : High, 25 over 5 is 5.0, clears all at 4.0
    CapacityRatio : nitrogen_capacity = ratio, below 1.0
    CapacityRatio : Medium 0.625, Low 0.375

    CapacityOne --> ActualGrowth
    CapacityOne2 --> ActualGrowth
    CapacityRatio --> ActualGrowth

    ActualGrowth : actual_growth function
    ActualGrowth : realized growth equals potential growth times the smaller of sugar_storage and nitrogen_capacity
    ActualGrowth --> [*]
</pre>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js"></script>
<script>mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:true});</script>
')
```

`potential growth` here comes from `growth.cpp`, driven purely by
temperature and phenology - it never sees carbon or nitrogen. Both
resources only enter at the `actual_growth()` step above, as a cap on that
potential.

**The genuine feedback loop** (`organ_level_sugar = TRUE`, exercised in
Section 4 below): growth actually consumes nitrogen and uptake has to
replenish it - this is the "uptake and all that jazz." Each
day, realized growth is converted to an N cost per organ (tissue N-content
constants from Korhonen 2013, divided by an assumed 0.5 C-content
fraction to get N:C), and `nitrogen_balance` is debited by that cost and
credited by `uptake.total_uptake`:

```{r nitrogen-uptake-diagram, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('
<pre class="mermaid">
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NitrogenBalance
    NitrogenBalance --> NitrogenConsumed : growth times organ N to C ratio, summed across organs
    NitrogenConsumed --> RootUptake
    NitrogenConsumed --> MycoUptake
    RootUptake : saturating function of root biomass and a fixed soil N value of 0.5
    MycoUptake : saturating function of myco biomass and soil N, scaled by sugar paid to the fungus
    RootUptake --> TotalUptake
    MycoUptake --> TotalUptake
    TotalUptake --> NitrogenBalance : balance increases by uptake minus consumed, carried to next day
    NitrogenBalance --> [*]
</pre>
')
```

Notes on this loop (`nitrogen_uptake()`, `sugar_model.cpp:208-248`): the
soil-N input (`N = 0.5`) is a hardcoded placeholder, not read from real
soil data or from `nitrogen_balance` itself - it's marked `TODO` in the
source (`root_biomass`/`mycorrhizal_biomass` from the *previous* day).
Root uptake is throttled by `free_sugar_percentage` (uptake needs "free"
sugar the tree hasn't already committed to the mycorrhiza); mycorrhizal
transfer is a saturating function of how much sugar the tree pays the
fungus - a genuine carbon-for-nitrogen trade. Note uptake itself never
responds to how full `nitrogen_balance` already is - only to biomass and
that fixed soil-N constant - which is why the pool only ever grows in
Section 4's runs; a down-regulation fix for this was considered and
deliberately deferred there. One bug spotted while first tracing this -
immediately after the balance update, `sugar_model.cpp` used to set
`nitrogen_capacity.height = nitrogen_balance` directly, skipping
`nitrogen_storage()` entirely - **has since been fixed** (Section 4.2),
along with every organ-level capacity call passing the shared `"all"`
placeholder instead of its own organ and the raw (undivided) balance.

## 3  Nitrogen scenarios

Same three constant nitrogen levels as `sugar_calibration.Rmd` (30/50/100%
of the baseline 25 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), on the default (whole-tree) sugar
pathway, plus an unconstrained Control.

`nitrogen_change = TRUE` is required for `nitrogen_balance` to actually be
read (see note below) - with it `FALSE`, the model always treats nitrogen
as non-limiting regardless of `nitrogen_balance`'s value, which is why
Control uses `nitrogen_change = FALSE` and the three levels use `TRUE`.

```{r run-nitrogen}
run_nitrogen <- function(nitrogen_balance, nitrogen_change = FALSE,
                         nitrogen_contrast = FALSE) {
  CASSIA_cpp(
    weather                 = weather_1998_2022,
    site                    = "Hyde",
    pPREL                   = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
    parameters              = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
    common                  = common_p,
    ratios                  = ratios_p,
    sperling                = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
    needle_mass_in          = 0,
    Throughfall             = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
    photosynthesis_as_input = FALSE,
    nitrogen_balance        = nitrogen_balance,
    nitrogen_change         = nitrogen_change,
    nitrogen_contrast       = nitrogen_contrast,
    preles                  = TRUE,
    fAPAR_Tian              = TRUE,
    organ_level_sugar       = FALSE,
    needle_mass_grows       = TRUE
  )
}

n_cols <- c(Control = "#4d4d4d", High = "#1b7837",
           Medium = "#e08214", Low = "#377eb8")

CASSIA_control  <- run_nitrogen(25,          nitrogen_change = FALSE)
CASSIA_N_high   <- run_nitrogen(25,          nitrogen_change = TRUE)
CASSIA_N_medium <- run_nitrogen(25 * 0.5,    nitrogen_change = TRUE)
CASSIA_N_low    <- run_nitrogen(25 * 0.3,    nitrogen_change = TRUE)
```

### 3.1  Height and diameter under Control/high/medium/low nitrogen

```{r plot-n-clean, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9}
height_n_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_control$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,  N = "Control"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_high$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,   N = "High"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_medium$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height, N = "Medium"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_low$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,    N = "Low")
)
height_n_long$N <- factor(height_n_long$N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))

diameter_n_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_control$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,  N = "Control"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_high$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,   N = "High"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_medium$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter, N = "Medium"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022,
             value = CASSIA_N_low$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,    N = "Low")
)
diameter_n_long$N <- factor(diameter_n_long$N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))

p_n_height <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = height_n_long, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = N),
            linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = transform(obs_height, N = "Observed"),
             aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = "Observed"),
             shape = 17, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(n_cols, Observed = obs_col)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(12, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Height", x = NULL, y = "Height (m)") +
  pub_theme

final_height_n <- aggregate(value ~ N, data = height_n_long,
                            FUN = function(x) tail(x, 1))
obs_final_height_n <- tail(obs_height$value, 1)

p_n_height_final <- ggplot(final_height_n, aes(x = N, y = value, fill = N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = obs_final_height_n, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = obs_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = obs_final_height_n, label = "Observed (2022)",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, colour = obs_col, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = n_cols) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(12, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Final height (2022)", x = NULL, y = "Height (m)") +
  pub_theme

p_n_diameter <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = diameter_n_long, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = N),
            linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = transform(obs_diameter, N = "Observed"),
             aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = "Observed"),
             shape = 17, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(n_cols, Observed = obs_col)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Diameter", x = NULL, y = "Diameter (m)") +
  pub_theme

final_diameter_n <- aggregate(value ~ N, data = diameter_n_long,
                              FUN = function(x) tail(x, 1))
obs_final_diameter_n <- tail(obs_diameter$value, 1)

p_n_diameter_final <- ggplot(final_diameter_n, aes(x = N, y = value, fill = N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = obs_final_diameter_n, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = obs_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = obs_final_diameter_n, label = "Observed (2022)",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, colour = obs_col, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = n_cols) +
  labs(title = "Final diameter (2022)", x = NULL, y = "Diameter (m)") +
  pub_theme

row_height   <- (p_n_height   | p_n_height_final)   + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))
row_diameter <- (p_n_diameter | p_n_diameter_final) + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))

(row_height / row_diameter) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Height and diameter under Control/high/medium/low nitrogen, 1998–2022",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15))
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**Why High ≈ Control but Medium/Low differ.** `nitrogen_storage()`
(`sugar_model.cpp`) compares `nitrogen_balance/5` against a fixed organ
capacity of 4.0: High (25/5 = 5.0) clears that capacity and is capped at
1.0 - i.e. unconstrained, same as Control. Medium (12.5/5 = 2.5 → 0.625)
and Low (7.5/5 = 1.5 → 0.375) fall under it, so they genuinely throttle
growth via `actual_growth()`'s `std::min(sugar_storage, nitrogen_capacity)`
gate. `nitrogen_balance` itself is never updated in this (non-organ-level)
pathway - it's a fixed input for the whole run, not a depleting pool -
so each scenario applies one constant daily multiplier throughout.
See `manuscript/paper_plan.Rmd` (Working notes, "Nitrogen limitation
outside the sugar model") for the earlier, less complete account of this
and a proposal for extending it. Section 4 below carries out that
extension - same nitrogen levels, organ-level pathway.

## 4  Nitrogen scenarios + organ-level sugar model (within-year dynamics)

Section 3 only exercises the whole-tree capacity gate, where
`nitrogen_balance` is a frozen input and `uptake` never moves (Section 2).
Switching to `organ_level_sugar = TRUE` activates the real feedback loop:
`nitrogen_balance` is credited by root + mycorrhizal uptake and debited by
the organ nitrogen-cost of realized growth every day, so it genuinely
evolves within a year and across years. This section reruns the same four
nitrogen levels as Section 3 on that pathway to see what those dynamics
actually look like.

### 4.1  Running the organ-level pathway

```{r run-nitrogen-organ}
run_nitrogen_organ <- function(nitrogen_balance, nitrogen_change = FALSE,
                               nitrogen_contrast = FALSE) {
  CASSIA_cpp(
    weather                 = weather_1998_2022,
    site                    = "Hyde",
    pPREL                   = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
    parameters              = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
    common                  = common_p,
    ratios                  = ratios_p,
    sperling                = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
    needle_mass_in          = 0,
    Throughfall             = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
    photosynthesis_as_input = FALSE,
    nitrogen_balance        = nitrogen_balance,
    nitrogen_change         = nitrogen_change,
    nitrogen_contrast       = nitrogen_contrast,
    preles                  = TRUE,
    fAPAR_Tian              = TRUE,
    organ_level_sugar       = TRUE,
    needle_mass_grows       = TRUE
  )
}

CASSIA_control_organ  <- run_nitrogen_organ(25,          nitrogen_change = FALSE)
CASSIA_N_high_organ   <- run_nitrogen_organ(25,          nitrogen_change = TRUE)
CASSIA_N_medium_organ <- run_nitrogen_organ(25 * 0.5,    nitrogen_change = TRUE)
CASSIA_N_low_organ    <- run_nitrogen_organ(25 * 0.3,    nitrogen_change = TRUE)

# Pulls the per-day nitrogen columns into one long table. `Uptake` is only
# present as a list element when nitrogen_change = TRUE (CASSIA.cpp:563-569),
# so Control (nitrogen_change = FALSE) gets zero-filled instead.
extract_n_daily <- function(res, N_label, dates) {
  total_uptake <- if (!is.null(res$Uptake)) res$Uptake$total_uptake else rep(0, length(dates))
  data.table::data.table(
    dates             = dates,
    N                 = N_label,
    nitrogen_balance  = res$Sugar$nitrogen_balance,
    nitrogen_capacity = res$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_needles,
    total_uptake      = total_uptake
  )
}
```

### 4.2  Two fixes applied: organ-specific thresholds, and a pool that still only grows

Two bugs from the first pass of this notebook have since been fixed
directly in `sugar_model.cpp`, based on the intended design: the nitrogen
store is meant to be split evenly across the 5 pools (needles/bud/wall/
height/roots), with each organ compared against its own tissue N-content
threshold, not a shared placeholder.

1. **Organ-specific thresholds, evenly split** (`sugar_model.cpp:397-405`).
   Every call used to pass the same hardcoded `"all"` organ (4.0,
   `// TODO: Average of the biomass`) and the raw, undivided
   `nitrogen_balance`. Now each organ passes its own name and
   `nitrogen_balance/5.0` - the same even-split convention the whole-tree
   branch already used (`sugar_model.cpp:883`) - so needles/bud/wall/
   height/roots are compared against their own Korhonen 2007 constants
   (4.9/2.1/4.5/4.5/3.0 mg N g⁻¹, `sugar_model.cpp:119-132`) instead of
   one shared, uncalibrated number.
2. **Height capacity is no longer overwritten.** A line directly after
   the balance update used to set `nitrogen_capacity.height` back to the
   raw, unclipped `nitrogen_balance` (the bug flagged in Section 2),
   silently undoing fix 1 for height specifically. That line is removed,
   so height now goes through the same `nitrogen_storage()` clipping as
   every other organ.

```{r n-scaling-check}
n_scaling_check <- data.frame(
  N = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"),
  min_needles = c(min(CASSIA_control_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_needles),
                  min(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_needles),
                  min(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_needles),
                  min(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_needles)),
  min_wall    = c(min(CASSIA_control_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_wall),
                  min(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_wall),
                  min(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_wall),
                  min(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_wall)),
  min_height  = c(min(CASSIA_control_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_height),
                  min(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_height),
                  min(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_height),
                  min(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_height)),
  min_roots   = c(min(CASSIA_control_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_roots),
                  min(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_roots),
                  min(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_roots),
                  min(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_capacity_roots)),
  final_balance = c(tail(CASSIA_control_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_balance, 1),
                     tail(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_balance, 1),
                     tail(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_balance, 1),
                     tail(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Sugar$nitrogen_balance, 1)),
  final_height = c(tail(CASSIA_control_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height, 1),
                    tail(CASSIA_N_high_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height, 1),
                    tail(CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height, 1),
                    tail(CASSIA_N_low_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height, 1))
)
knitr::kable(n_scaling_check, digits = 4)
```

This is a real change: capacity now genuinely differs by organ and by
scenario (Low dips to needles ≈ 0.31, wall/height ≈ 0.33, roots ≈ 0.50 -
bud barely dips at all, since its threshold, `2.1/5 = 0.42` on the raw
balance, is the easiest of the five to clear). Medium shows a smaller
version of the same pattern; High and Control never throttle at all.

**But it's still confined to year 1.** Checking when each organ's
capacity last drops below 1.0: for Low, needles is throttled on and off
through 1998-09-15 (2.8% of days over the full 25 years), roots through
1998-06-07 (1.7%) - every single throttled day falls in 1998, the first
year of the run. `nitrogen_balance` still only ever grows (uptake is
driven by root/mycorrhizal biomass, not by how full the pool already is
- Section 2 - so there's still no feedback making it shrink; that fix was
considered and deliberately deferred, Section 4.5). The organ-specific
thresholds are higher than the old flat 4.0 (effectively 10.5 to 24.5 on
the raw balance, `5 ×` each organ's constant), so it takes longer to
escape them than before the fix - but escape is still what happens, once
and permanently, partway through year 1. The other 24 years run
completely unconstrained regardless of starting level.

Net effect on the headline growth variables: Low's final height comes out
**0.0004 m** below Control's (12.994430 m vs 12.994822 m) after 25 years -
a real, non-zero, nitrogen-driven difference for the first time in this
notebook - and diameter is unchanged to 6 decimal places even for Low.
Both fixes are working as intended; there just isn't much growing season
left in year 1 by the time Low's threshold is crossed, and nothing after
year 1 is ever nitrogen-limited again.

### 4.3  Height/diameter: a tiny, real effect for Low only

```{r plot-n-organ-heightdiam, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
height_n_long_organ <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_control_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,  N = "Control"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_high_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,    N = "High"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,  N = "Medium"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_low_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_height,     N = "Low")
)
height_n_long_organ$N <- factor(height_n_long_organ$N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))

diameter_n_long_organ <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_control_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,  N = "Control"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_high_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,   N = "High"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_medium_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter, N = "Medium"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_N_low_organ$Culm_Growth$culm_growth_diameter,    N = "Low")
)
diameter_n_long_organ$N <- factor(diameter_n_long_organ$N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))

p_n_height_organ <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = height_n_long_organ, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = N),
            linewidth = 1.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = transform(obs_height, N = "Observed"),
             aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = "Observed"),
             shape = 17, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(n_cols, Observed = obs_col)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(12, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Height - Low ends ~0.4mm below the rest; Control/High/Medium overlap exactly",
       x = NULL, y = "Height (m)") +
  pub_theme

p_n_diameter_organ <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = diameter_n_long_organ, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = N),
            linewidth = 1.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = transform(obs_diameter, N = "Observed"),
             aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = "Observed"),
             shape = 17, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(n_cols, Observed = obs_col)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Diameter - identical to 6 decimal places, even for Low",
       x = NULL, y = "Diameter (m)") +
  pub_theme

(p_n_height_organ / p_n_diameter_organ) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### 4.4  Within-year and across-year nitrogen pool dynamics

Section 4.2 found a real but brief effect on growth (year 1 only). This
section looks at the per-day dynamics behind that - what "within-year
nitrogen" looks like in the organ-level pathway now that capacity is
genuinely organ-specific.

```{r n-daily-all}
n_daily_all <- rbind(
  extract_n_daily(CASSIA_control_organ,  "Control", dates_1998_2022),
  extract_n_daily(CASSIA_N_high_organ,   "High",    dates_1998_2022),
  extract_n_daily(CASSIA_N_medium_organ, "Medium",  dates_1998_2022),
  extract_n_daily(CASSIA_N_low_organ,    "Low",     dates_1998_2022)
)
n_daily_all[, N := factor(N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))]
n_daily_all[, doy  := as.integer(format(dates, "%j"))]
n_daily_all[, year := as.integer(format(dates, "%Y"))]
n_daily_all <- n_daily_all[order(N, dates)]

# nitrogen_balance logs as 0 on the very first day of the whole run (a
# logging-order artifact, not a real model value - log_sugar() runs before
# the first day's balance update) - drop that one row per scenario so it
# doesn't distort the derived "consumed" series below.
n_daily_all <- n_daily_all[!(dates == min(dates))]

# Daily nitrogen consumed by growth isn't logged directly - derive it from
# the balance update itself (balance_t = balance_t-1 + uptake_t - consumed_t,
# sugar_model.cpp:589-605), i.e. consumed = uptake - the day's change in balance.
n_daily_all[, consumed := total_uptake - (nitrogen_balance - shift(nitrogen_balance)), by = N]
```

```{r plot-n-seasonal, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 11}
n_seasonal_long <- data.table::melt(
  n_daily_all,
  id.vars       = c("dates", "N", "doy", "year"),
  measure.vars  = c("nitrogen_balance", "total_uptake", "consumed", "nitrogen_capacity"),
  variable.name = "metric", value.name = "value"
)
n_seasonal_long[, metric := factor(metric,
  levels = c("nitrogen_balance", "total_uptake", "consumed", "nitrogen_capacity"),
  labels = c("Nitrogen balance (pool)", "Total uptake (daily)",
             "Consumed by growth (daily, derived)", "Nitrogen capacity (needles)"))]

p_n_seasonal <- ggplot(n_seasonal_long, aes(x = doy, y = value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = year), colour = "grey65", alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ N, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Within-year nitrogen dynamics, organ-level pathway",
    subtitle = "Each grey line is one year (1998-2022); black line is the across-year mean by day of year",
    x = "Day of year", y = NULL
  ) +
  pub_theme +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

p_n_seasonal
```

Reading this grid: **uptake** and **consumed** show a genuine seasonal
pulse (near zero in winter, rising through the growing season) because
both track phenology/biomass - that part of the day-of-year aggregate is
meaningful. **Capacity** (needles, as one representative organ) is 1.0
for the overwhelming majority of days - the real throttling found in
Section 4.2 is genuine but confined to roughly the first 8 months of a
25-year run, so it's a thin sliver of grey lines near the bottom of that
panel rather than a visible dip in the black across-year mean; Low's
other throttled organs (wall/height/roots) show the same pattern.
**Balance** is the odd one out: it isn't a repeating seasonal variable at
all, it's a running total that ratchets up every year, so a day-of-year
average mixes together 25 different (and rising) baseline levels - the
shape above is dominated by that drift, not by a within-year pattern.
Control stays flat at 25 throughout (as a constant
`nitrogen_change = FALSE` input - see Section 2); High/Medium/Low all
climb. The trend panel below makes that explicit.

```{r plot-n-trend, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
n_annual <- n_daily_all[, .(mean_balance = mean(nitrogen_balance, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(N, year)]

p_n_trend <- ggplot(n_annual, aes(x = year, y = mean_balance, colour = N)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = n_cols) +
  labs(
    title = "Long-run trend: annual mean nitrogen_balance, 1998-2022",
    subtitle = "What the day-of-year aggregate above hides - Control stays fixed, the other three balloon and converge",
    x = NULL, y = "Nitrogen balance (pool)"
  ) +
  pub_theme

p_n_trend
```

### 4.5  Demonstrating the mechanism directly: a diagnostic low-nitrogen run

High and Control never throttle at all, and Medium/Low only do so
briefly in year 1 (Section 4.2). One extra run, starting well below even
needles' threshold (`5 × 4.9 = 24.5` on the raw balance, Section 4.2),
shows the capacity gate's full ramp more clearly.

```{r run-n-diagnostic}
CASSIA_N_stress_organ <- run_nitrogen_organ(1, nitrogen_change = TRUE)
n_stress_daily <- extract_n_daily(CASSIA_N_stress_organ, "Stress", dates_1998_2022)
n_stress_daily <- n_stress_daily[dates <= as.Date("1999-12-31")]
```

```{r plot-n-diagnostic, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
p_diag_balance <- ggplot(n_stress_daily, aes(x = dates, y = nitrogen_balance)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 24.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = min(n_stress_daily$dates), y = 24.5, label = "needles threshold = 24.5 (5 x 4.9)",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "nitrogen_balance", x = NULL, y = "nitrogen_balance") +
  pub_theme

p_diag_capacity <- ggplot(n_stress_daily, aes(x = dates, y = nitrogen_capacity)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Resulting nitrogen_capacity (needles)", x = NULL, y = "capacity (0-1)") +
  pub_theme

(p_diag_balance | p_diag_capacity) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Diagnostic: starting at nitrogen_balance = 1 (well below needles' 24.5 threshold)",
    subtitle = "Capacity starts at 0.04 and ramps up slowly, crossing 1.0 only in mid-November 1998 - then it clears permanently for the rest of the run",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
  )
```

Starting more than an order of magnitude below Low now buys most of a
full year of real nitrogen limitation (capacity climbs from 0.04 and
doesn't cross 1.0 until day 317, 1998-11-13 - 3.5% of all days across the
25-year run) - longer than before the Tier 1 fix, since the organ-specific
thresholds are higher than the old flat 4.0. But the ending is the same:
uptake (driven by biomass, not by the balance level itself) is large
enough that the pool crosses the threshold eventually and then - per
Section 4.2 - never comes back down; the other 24 years are completely
unconstrained regardless of how low the starting level was. Organ-
specific thresholds (this section) changed *how long* nitrogen matters;
they didn't change *that* it stops mattering after year 1. The natural
next step is the one considered and deliberately left for later: making
uptake itself down-regulate as the pool fills, so it can actually shrink
instead of only ever growing.

### 4.6  Actual growth and sugar/starch: more within-year dynamics

Section 4.4 looked at the nitrogen side (balance/uptake/consumed/
capacity). The same day-of-year treatment applied to the *carbon* side -
actual daily growth (not the cumulative `culm_growth_*` totals plotted in
4.3) and the whole-tree sugar/starch pools - shows what's actually
driving height and diameter, given Section 4.2's finding that nitrogen
is only a brief, minor factor (Low, year 1): `height_growth`/
`diameter_growth` are daily realized increments
from the `Growth` data frame (`output_functions.cpp:19-23`), and
`sugar`/`starch` are the whole-tree carbon pools from `Sugar`
(`output_functions.cpp:35-70`).

```{r growth-sugar-daily}
extract_growth_sugar_daily <- function(res, N_label, dates) {
  data.table::data.table(
    dates           = dates,
    N               = N_label,
    height_growth   = res$Growth$height_growth,
    diameter_growth = res$Growth$diameter_growth,
    sugar           = res$Sugar$sugar,
    starch          = res$Sugar$starch
  )
}

gs_daily_all <- rbind(
  extract_growth_sugar_daily(CASSIA_control_organ,  "Control", dates_1998_2022),
  extract_growth_sugar_daily(CASSIA_N_high_organ,   "High",    dates_1998_2022),
  extract_growth_sugar_daily(CASSIA_N_medium_organ, "Medium",  dates_1998_2022),
  extract_growth_sugar_daily(CASSIA_N_low_organ,    "Low",     dates_1998_2022)
)
gs_daily_all[, N := factor(N, levels = c("Control", "High", "Medium", "Low"))]
gs_daily_all[, doy  := as.integer(format(dates, "%j"))]
gs_daily_all[, year := as.integer(format(dates, "%Y"))]
```

```{r plot-growth-sugar-seasonal, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 11}
gs_seasonal_long <- data.table::melt(
  gs_daily_all,
  id.vars       = c("dates", "N", "doy", "year"),
  measure.vars  = c("height_growth", "diameter_growth", "sugar", "starch"),
  variable.name = "metric", value.name = "value"
)
gs_seasonal_long[, metric := factor(metric,
  levels = c("height_growth", "diameter_growth", "sugar", "starch"),
  labels = c("Height growth (daily, actual)", "Diameter growth (daily, actual)",
             "Sugar (whole-tree pool)", "Starch (whole-tree pool)"))]

p_gs_seasonal <- ggplot(gs_seasonal_long, aes(x = doy, y = value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = year), colour = "grey65", alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ N, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Actual growth and carbon pools, organ-level pathway",
    subtitle = "Each grey line is one year (1998-2022); black line is the across-year mean by day of year",
    x = "Day of year", y = NULL
  ) +
  pub_theme +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

p_gs_seasonal
```

Growth is a clean seasonal pulse (zero through winter dormancy, rising
and falling with the growing season) - this is the `g`-driven phenology
from `growth.cpp` (Section 2), gated by carbon via `actual_growth()`.
Sugar and starch show the expected annual cycle too: sugar builds up
through the photosynthetic season and starch accumulates as a winter
reserve, repeating each year rather than drifting the way
`nitrogen_balance` does - carbon is a genuine annually-cycling pool here
in a way nitrogen (in this pathway, at these levels) is not. Consistent
with Section 4.2, the four panels are visually indistinguishable between
Control/High/Medium/Low within each row at this scale - Low's real but
~0.4mm-over-25-years effect on height (Section 4.2-4.3) is too small to
see in a plot built from 25 years of daily values, even though it is
there in the underlying numbers.
